title: ACHONDROPLASIA, SEVERE, WITH DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY AND ACANTHOSIS NIGRICANS

relationships.phenotype: ACHONDROPLASIA, SEVERE, WITH DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY AND ACANTHOSIS NIGRICANS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans (SADDAN) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the FGFR3 gene (134934) on chromosome 4p16.3.

checks.claim: Severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans (SADDAN) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the FGFR3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We refer to the phenotype caused by the Lys650Met mutation as "severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans" (SADDAN)
checks.explanation: The abstract says an FGFR3 mutation causes SADDAN, but it does not say the mutation is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 gene is located on chromosome 4p16.3.
checks.evidence_quote: fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) missense mutation
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that restates the gene the paper names.

paragraphs.text: SADDAN is a rare, severe skeletal dysplasia caused by an activating mutation in FGFR3. Its main features are severe short-limbed short stature with bowing of the long bones, marked developmental delay, and acanthosis nigricans that appears in childhood. The skeletal findings resemble thanatophoric dysplasia, but some affected individuals have survived past infancy.

checks.claim: SADDAN is a rare, severe skeletal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: skeletal dysplasia that approaches the severity observed in thanatophoric dysplasia type I (TD1)
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a severe, novel skeletal dysplasia, but it does not call it rare.

checks.claim: SADDAN is caused by an activating mutation in FGFR3.
checks.evidence_quote: the Lys650Met mutation causes a dramatic increase in constitutive receptor kinase activity
checks.explanation: A dramatic increase in constitutive kinase activity means the mutation is activating.

checks.claim: A main feature of SADDAN is severe short-limbed short stature with bowing of the long bones.
checks.evidence_quote: Other unusual bone deformities, such as femoral bowing with reverse (i.e., posterior apex) tibial and fibular bowing and "ram's horn" bowing of the clavicle, are also seen in some patients.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes severe disturbances of bone growth and bowing in some patients, but not short-limbed short stature as a main feature.

checks.claim: A main feature of SADDAN is marked developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: suffer from severe neurological impairments
checks.explanation: Developmental delay is also part of the disorder's name in the paper.

checks.claim: A main feature of SADDAN is acanthosis nigricans that appears in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: developed extensive areas of acanthosis nigricans beginning in early childhood
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The skeletal findings of SADDAN resemble those of thanatophoric dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: severe disturbances in endochondral bone growth that approach and overlap those observed in thanatophoric dysplasia, type I
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the skeletal findings overlap with thanatophoric dysplasia type I.

checks.evidence_quote: have survived past infancy without prolonged life-support measures
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Tavormina et al. (1999) reported unrelated individuals with a skeletal dysplasia that they named SADDAN. Patients had severe short stature with marked bowing of the femur and tibia, profound developmental delay, and acanthosis nigricans that developed in early childhood. Radiographic features were similar to those of thanatophoric dysplasia type I, but some patients survived beyond infancy, in some cases without long-term ventilatory support. Some patients also had seizures, hydrocephalus, and structural central nervous system abnormalities.

paragraphs.text: The mutations reported in SADDAN arose de novo and were present in the heterozygous state, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance (Tavormina et al., 1999).

checks.explanation: The abstract does not say the mutations arose de novo.

checks.explanation: The abstract does not state zygosity.

checks.explanation: The abstract does not discuss the mode of inheritance.

paragraphs.text: In unrelated patients with SADDAN, Tavormina et al. (1999) identified a heterozygous c.1949A-T transversion in the FGFR3 gene. The change caused a lys650-to-met (K650M) substitution in the activation loop of the tyrosine kinase domain. In transfection studies, the K650M receptor showed strong ligand-independent constitutive kinase activity.

checks.claim: Tavormina et al. (1999) identified a heterozygous c.1949A-T transversion in the FGFR3 gene in unrelated patients with SADDAN.
checks.evidence_quote: The FGFR3 mutation (A1949T: Lys650Met)
checks.explanation: The abstract reports the A1949T mutation in four unrelated individuals, but it does not say the mutation is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 c.1949A-T transversion results in a lys650-to-met (K650M) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: The FGFR3 mutation (A1949T: Lys650Met)
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 K650M substitution lies in the activation loop of the tyrosine kinase domain.
checks.evidence_quote: at a highly conserved codon in the kinase domain activation loop
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In transfection studies, the FGFR3 K650M receptor showed strong ligand-independent constitutive kinase activity.
checks.evidence_quote: Transient transfection studies with FGFR3 mutant constructs show that the Lys650Met mutation causes a dramatic increase in constitutive receptor kinase activity
checks.explanation: A dramatic increase in constitutive kinase activity matches strong ligand-independent activity.

paragraphs.text: Bellus et al. (2000) compared mutations at FGFR3 codon lys650. The K650M mutation found in SADDAN activated the receptor kinase much more strongly than the K650E mutation found in thanatophoric dysplasia type II, which in turn was more activating than the milder K650N and K650Q substitutions found in hypochondroplasia. The authors concluded that the degree of receptor activation correlated with the severity of the skeletal phenotype. Bellus et al. (2000) also noted that the K650M mutation had been found in some patients diagnosed with thanatophoric dysplasia type I.

checks.claim: Bellus et al. (2000) compared mutations at FGFR3 codon lys650.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. This claim is about Bellus et al. (2000), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 K650M mutation found in SADDAN activated the receptor kinase much more strongly than the FGFR3 K650E mutation found in thanatophoric dysplasia type II, per Bellus et al. (2000).
checks.evidence_quote: However, FGFR3 with the SADDAN mutation is more activated than FGFR3 with the TDII mutation in vitro.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the SADDAN mutation is more activating than the TDII mutation. It does not say 'much more' and does not attribute the finding to Bellus et al.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 K650E mutation found in thanatophoric dysplasia type II was more activating than the FGFR3 K650N and K650Q substitutions found in hypochondroplasia, per Bellus et al. (2000).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The abstract does not mention K650N, K650Q or hypochondroplasia.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 K650N and K650Q substitutions are found in hypochondroplasia and are milder.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The abstract does not mention hypochondroplasia mutations.

checks.claim: Bellus et al. (2000) concluded that the degree of FGFR3 receptor activation correlated with the severity of the skeletal phenotype.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. This is a conclusion of Bellus et al. (2000) and is not in this abstract.

checks.claim: Bellus et al. (2000) noted that the FGFR3 K650M mutation had been found in some patients diagnosed with thanatophoric dysplasia type I.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. This is a statement by Bellus et al. (2000) and is not in this abstract.

paragraphs.text: Bellus et al. (2000) found that different amino acid substitutions at FGFR3 lys650 caused different levels of constitutive kinase activation. These levels corresponded to a phenotypic spectrum, from hypochondroplasia (K650N/Q) to thanatophoric dysplasia type II (K650E) and SADDAN (K650M).

checks.claim: Bellus et al. (2000) found that different amino acid substitutions at FGFR3 lys650 caused different levels of constitutive kinase activation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. This is a finding of Bellus et al. (2000); this abstract compares only K650M with K650E.

checks.claim: Per Bellus et al. (2000), the levels of constitutive kinase activation caused by FGFR3 lys650 substitutions corresponded to a phenotypic spectrum from hypochondroplasia (K650N/Q) to thanatophoric dysplasia type II (K650E) and SADDAN (K650M).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. This is a finding of Bellus et al. (2000); this abstract does not mention hypochondroplasia or a phenotypic spectrum.

paragraphs.text: In unrelated patients with SADDAN, Tavormina et al. (1999) identified a heterozygous de novo c.1949A-T transversion in the FGFR3 gene, resulting in a lys650-to-met (K650M) substitution in the kinase domain activation loop. The mutant receptor showed strong constitutive kinase activation. Bellus et al. (2000) showed that K650M was more strongly activating than the K650E mutation that causes thanatophoric dysplasia type II.

checks.claim: Tavormina et al. (1999) identified a heterozygous c.1949A-T transversion in the FGFR3 gene in unrelated patients with SADDAN.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified a novel fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) missense mutation in four unrelated individuals
checks.explanation: The abstract identifies the mutation (A1949T) in four unrelated individuals but does not state that it is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 c.1949A-T transversion in SADDAN patients occurred de novo.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not say the mutation arose de novo.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 c.1949A-T transversion results in a lys650-to-met (K650M) substitution in the kinase domain activation loop.
checks.evidence_quote: The FGFR3 mutation (A1949T: Lys650Met) occurs at the nucleotide adjacent to the TD type II (TD2) mutation (A1948G: Lys650Glu) and results in a different amino acid substitution at a highly conserved codon in the kinase domain activation loop.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The FGFR3 K650M mutant receptor showed strong constitutive kinase activation.
checks.evidence_quote: the Lys650Met mutation causes a dramatic increase in constitutive receptor kinase activity
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Bellus et al. (2000) showed that FGFR3 K650M was more strongly activating than the FGFR3 K650E mutation that causes thanatophoric dysplasia type II.
checks.explanation: The claim is attributed to Bellus et al. (2000), which this paper does not address. This paper itself reports K650M activity about 3 times greater than K650E.
